prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key policies and proposals (2017 manifesto)

Brexit and trade
- Seek a “deep and special” partnership with the EU; leave the single market and customs union; Great Repeal Bill to convert EU law into UK law.
- Maintain workers’, consumer and environmental protections at exit; frictionless Irish border; protect rights of EU/UK citizens.
- Replicate existing EU trade deals, lodge WTO schedules, introduce a Trade Bill; create Trade Commissioners and reconvene the Board of Trade.

Economy, tax and regulation
- Balance the budget by the mid-2020s; keep taxes low: personal allowance to £12,500 and higher rate threshold to £50,000 by 2020; no rise in VAT; corporation tax to 17%.
- Reform business rates, simplify tax system, reduce regulatory burden; review utility and infrastructure regulation for value.
- National Productivity Investment Fund (£23bn) for housing, R&D, infrastructure, skills; increase R&D to 2.4% of GDP within 10 years (goal 3%).
- “Future Britain” sovereign-style funds; SME procurement target of 33%.

Work, pay and corporate governance
- Increase National Living Wage to 60% of median by 2020; act on gig-economy protections after the Taylor Review.
- Tougher action on tax evasion; stronger pension regulation (fines, director disqualification, potential criminal offence).
- Tighten takeover rules; protect critical infrastructure; shareholder votes on executive pay, publish pay ratios; employee representation options on boards; Prompt Payment enforcement.

Energy, industry, and infrastructure
- Independent Cost of Energy review; diverse energy mix; expand offshore wind; enable shale gas with a single regulator and community benefit fund.
- Invest in HS2, Northern Powerhouse Rail, Heathrow expansion; EVs: nearly all cars/vans zero-emission by 2050; cycling and local transport upgrades.

Devolution, communities, environment
- Strengthen the union; growth deals in Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland; relocate civil service and cultural bodies outside London.
- Create a UK Shared Prosperity Fund to replace EU structural funds.
- Maintain farm-support cash total this parliament; design new agri‑environment system next parliament; animal welfare measures; 25‑year environment plan.

Security, defence, justice, democracy
- Meet/exceed NATO 2% with real-terms increases; retain nuclear deterrent; £178bn equipment plan; veterans’ employment and services.
- Create a national infrastructure police force; fold the Serious Fraud Office into the NCA; enhance cyber security.
- Voter ID, boundary review to 600 MPs; repeal Fixed-term Parliaments Act; targeted Lords reform.
- Victims’ law; prison reform (10,000 places), stronger community sentences.

Immigration and integration
- Reduce net migration to “tens of thousands”; raise family visa income thresholds; tougher student visa rules; sectoral skills visas advised by MAC; double the Immigration Skills Charge.
- New integration strategy; Commission for Countering Extremism.

Education, skills and work
- 100 free schools per year; lift ban on selective schools (with conditions); require university/independent school sponsorship; expand specialist maths schools.
- School funding reform with no school losing under new formula; £4bn extra by 2022; free primary breakfasts replace universal infant lunches; EBacc expansion; teacher recruitment/retention support.
- Technical route: T-levels, 900 hours/yr and 3‑month placements; new institutes of technology; 3m apprenticeships; national retraining scheme; discounted travel for apprentices.

Health, social care, pensions
- NHS: at least £8bn real-terms increase over five years; expand workforce training; invest in buildings/technology; recover costs from non-residents; faster access to new treatments; seven‑day services; maintain A&E 95% and 18‑week targets; cancer 28‑day diagnosis; 10,000 more mental health staff.
- Social care: include home value in means test for home care; £100,000 asset floor; expand deferred payment to home care; carers’ leave; consult on system improvements.
- Pensions: retain triple lock to 2020, then “double lock”; align pension age with longevity; extend auto‑enrolment including to the self‑employed; means‑test Winter Fuel Payments to fund care.

Housing, families, and social policy
- Build 1.5m homes by 2022; protect Green Belt; 160,000 homes on public land; council housing deals with fixed terms and future Right to Buy; capture land value; CPO reform.
- 30 hours’ free childcare for 3–4 year‑olds in working families; expand nursery places; children’s mental health green paper; Domestic Violence and Abuse Bill; halve rough sleeping by 2022, end by 2027 (Housing First pilots).

Digital, data and media
- Digital Charter; support scale‑ups, IP protection, online consumer rights; broadband USO by 2020; full‑fibre/5G rollout; 95% geographic mobile coverage by 2022.
- Online safety measures for minors; stronger counter‑extremism online; new data protection law; youth “right to delete” at 18; Data Use & Ethics Commission; £1.9bn cyber programme.
- Digital government by default; Verify ID rollout; open data; geospatial data body; no Leveson 2; repeal Section 40.
